threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still avoid the buskers on Kingsland Road? Nah, you gotta learn to embrace the soundtrack of Dalston.
I once saw a guy on the 59 bus argue with his phone for ten minutes, then casually order a takeaway like it was the most normal thing ever.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a kid selling handmade lemonade on Sonnenallee, yelling '1 Euro for the secret recipe!' with the sun setting behind him.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how the U-Bahn stations here have names that sound like poetry? Warschauer Straße and Schlesisches Tor. They're like musical stops on your commute.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows the real reason the food trucks park at the same spot every Friday—it's the unofficial taco war meet-up.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full suit and tie eating a burrito while simultaneously reading a novel on Muni. Only in San Francisco do style and chaos coexist like that.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to the plaça, but miss the old bookshops hidden in the alleys. They're like treasure chests, full of stories and history.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they still carry a map in their hands, looking up bewildered at the corners of the Plaça del Sol.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when the bus driver asks for a contactless payment. Everyone else just flashes their card like it's second nature.
Last week on the 133, a guy in a suit tried to barter with the driver for a free ride after missing his stop. The driver just shook his head, classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Hearing a group of kids argue about which Kebab shop is the best while the scent of currywurst wafts through the street. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that doubles as an art gallery, where the walls are covered in local graffiti while you munch on döner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their reaction to BART delays—if they roll their eyes and keep scrolling on their phone, they’ve been through it all before.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a pigeon casually hopping onto the Muni seat, like it owned the place. The passengers barely blinked—classic San Francisco indifference.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the hipster bars, but the real charm is in the quiet afternoons at Plaça de la Vila watching local kids play.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their struggle to choose between 'barça' and 'català' when ordering coffee – they always look a bit lost.
